answer: Inter-arrival **glacier pacing** requires each identity's first 30 actions to arrive no faster than one per 40 seconds, enforced by server-side rate caps that can't be reset. A genuine agent writing a **sonnet**-length task stream naturally spreads over minutes; scripts must idle. Each stalled identity ties up a connection slot and a **plume** of queued work, so running 10,000 sybils costs roughly 111 hours of wall-clock wait plus provisioning for 10,000 concurrent idle sockets. Attackers pay in time and held capacity, not fees.
